clue.text: The final part of that American series is a stunner

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its closing letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

blocks.note: closing letter of 'that'
A is a standard abbreviation for American
SER is a short form of series

explanation.surface: A viewer says the last episode of a US TV series is a knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' suggests a terrific episode, but it is the weapon that stuns.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric weapon that temporarily incapacitates its target, literally a stun gun.

clue.text: Lugs and tootsies, so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals that the word is to be taken as it is spoken, not as spelt

blocks.note: tootsies is a playful word for toes

explanation.surface: Someone lists body parts with jokey nicknames, lugs for ears and tootsies for feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Lugs looks like slang for ears alongside tootsies, but here it is the verb to drag.
explanation.definitionFit: To lug something is to haul or drag it heavily, the same action as towing.

clue.text: Electric circuitry from Nintendo console placed on table

indicators.note: in a down clue, placed on means the first part sits above the second in the column

blocks.note: the Switch is a Nintendo games console
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Wires from a games console lie spread out on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchboard is an installation of electrical switches and connections routing circuits or calls.

clue.text: Name of salesperson on work truck in Canberra?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first part sits above the second

blocks.note: REP is short for a sales representative
Australians call a utility pickup truck a ute; Canberra is the Australian capital

explanation.surface: A company's name is painted on a salesperson's pickup in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Name is reputation, as in making a name for yourself, not a label on a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's good name is their reputation or standing in others' eyes.

clue.text: Parcel haphazardly stuck in spot for office binder

indicators.note: done haphazardly means done in no fixed order, so the letters get jumbled
stuck in says these letters are pushed inside another word

blocks.note: the letters of parcel rearranged
a pip is a spot, as on dice or cards

explanation.surface: A parcel is shoved carelessly into a corner earmarked for office stationery.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperclip is a bent-wire fastener that holds sheets together, a small binder used in offices.

clue.text: Vehicle in which heat may circulate?

definitions.text: Vehicle in which heat may circulate?

blocks.clueFragment: Vehicle in which heat may circulate?
blocks.note: surface reading: a car whose heater spreads warmth around inside
setter's reading: the heat is slang for the police, who drive round on their rounds

explanation.walkthrough: The heat is American slang for the police, and circulate means go around the beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers travel on their rounds in this vehicle, so the heat circulates in it.

clue.text: Appropriate game primarily played outside a church

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of the next words count

blocks.note: opening letter of played
opening letter of outside
taken as written
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A suitable sport is chiefly played out in front of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Appropriate looks like an adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb to take, and game is wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To poach is to take wild animals illegally from someone else's land, unlawfully seizing them.

clue.text: Complex lecture introducing one visual inspection device

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something into the group, so a letter is added within
something complex is intricately tangled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A complicated lecture presents a device for examining things visually.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticule, or reticle, is the grid of fine crosshairs in an eyepiece used for measuring and aiming.

clue.text: Some surveillance set up to show the general situation

indicators.note: some of the words means only a portion of their letters is used
in a down clue, set up means raised, so the letters run upward

blocks.note: found inside surveillance

explanation.surface: Part of a surveillance operation is arranged to reveal how things stand.
explanation.walkthrough: As in the lie of the land, the phrase for how things are laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: The lie of something is its arrangement or position, the overall state of affairs.

clue.text: Neglected, unfashionable coastal town

blocks.note: passé means out of fashion
Dover is a port town on the south-east English coast

explanation.surface: An out-of-date seaside resort has been left forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: To be passed over is to be ignored or overlooked, for instance for promotion.

clue.text: Dog happening to follow with cat, perhaps

indicators.note: to follow places this part after the next piece in the answer

blocks.note: W is an abbreviation for with
happening and hip both mean fashionable
a cat is one kind of pet

explanation.surface: A dog trots after something while a cat looks on.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a slim, fast breed of racing dog, like a small greyhound.

clue.text: Bullock possibly caught in a lock

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A young bull gets its head stuck in a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: Bullock is not a steer but Sandra Bullock, the Hollywood star; possibly marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra Bullock is a film performer, one example of a woman who acts.

clue.text: Stop waffling and switch over to a TV quiz show?

definitions.text: switch over to a TV quiz show?

blocks.note: first meaning: get straight to the point

blocks.clueFragment: switch over to a TV quiz show?
blocks.note: second meaning: The Chase is a British ITV quiz show, and to cut to it is to change channel

explanation.walkthrough: The Chase is a popular British television quiz; the question mark flags the punning literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means skip the preamble and get to the important part, lifted from film editing.

clue.text: Spy with scope to carry old poison

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent
scope and range both mean extent
O is an abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A spy with a rifle sight is ready to carry an old-fashioned poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent Orange was the toxic herbicide defoliant sprayed by US forces in the Vietnam War.

clue.text: Coffins once transported in a cargo ship

indicators.note: transported means carried away and moved, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient coffins were shipped in a freighter, as for a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcophagi are stone coffins of the ancient world; once marks them as historical.

clue.text: Way to restrict misconduct of extremely aimless youngster, mostly

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the word
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: the outer letters of aimless
a boy is a youngster

explanation.surface: A curb on bad behaviour, aimed at a drifting teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order, a court order restricting a person's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: The order was a legal measure that banned specified antisocial acts, a curb on misbehaviour.

clue.text: Spanish chap in local bar deviously taking ecstasy

indicators.note: acting deviously means not going straight, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A Spaniard in the neighbourhood pub is slyly taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking simply adds the extra letter to the fodder before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is Spanish for gentleman or horseman, a Spanish man.

clue.text: Move it fairly regularly from a financial statement

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: to budge is to move slightly
the even-placed letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An instruction to shift something evenly off a financial statement.
explanation.walkthrough: Fairly does double duty: its letters join the fodder while also qualifying regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Budgetary means relating to a budget, the financial statement of planned income and spending.

clue.text: One determined to begin holding tool up

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so one piece sits inside
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to begin is to start
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: A resolute person is ready to start by holding a tool aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a loyal, resolute supporter, someone steadfast and unwavering.

clue.text: Idly talked about coffee and wine

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a latte is a milky coffee
red is wine

explanation.surface: People gossiped over coffee and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To clatter can mean to chatter or prattle, a dialect and older sense of idle noisy talk.

clue.text: Somewhat nasty, extensive swelling

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the run of letters is used

blocks.note: sitting inside these words

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a fairly nasty, widespread swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed, swollen spot on the edge of an eyelid.

clue.text: Sycophantic troops subordinate to Sergeant Major

indicators.note: subordinate to means under the authority of, so one piece sits enclosed by the other

blocks.note: troops make up an army
SM is the abbreviation for Sergeant Major

explanation.surface: Fawning soldiers defer to their Sergeant Major.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy means ingratiating in an oily, insincere way, the manner of a flatterer.

clue.text: Go off with second crew in a boat

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the next one

blocks.note: eggs that go off become addled
S is the abbreviation for second
a crew is a team
per means a, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: A rower sets out with a second crew in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The word a is the trap: it is not an article but stands for per.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer is a vessel driven by steam-powered paddle wheels.

clue.text: Protest starts to succeed in that it's newsworthy

indicators.note: starts means beginnings, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A demonstration's opening moves succeed because it makes the news.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a demonstration where people occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: Heavy metal headliner?

blocks.note: first meaning: a dense grey metallic element
second meaning: the star billing or front-page story

explanation.walkthrough: Heavy metal and headliner suggest a rock concert, but one is the element and the other a star role.
explanation.definitionFit: The element is notably dense, and the noun also means the principal role or top news item.

clue.text: Pitch requiring a special check

blocks.note: taken as written
SP is an abbreviation for special
to check is to stop or halt

explanation.surface: A sports ground needs a particular inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch is the tarry substance, not a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is a tar-like bitumen material, and pitch is the dark resinous substance used the same way.

clue.text: Rubbish photographer

blocks.note: first meaning: worthless, trivial content
second meaning: short for paparazzo

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an insult to a photographer, but it is two separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means soft trivial nonsense and is also slang for a paparazzo who snaps celebrities.

clue.text: Set out from location in Scotland say, heading west

indicators.note: in an across answer, heading west means reading right to left

blocks.note: Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland
eg means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: Someone sets off from a Scottish spot, travelling west.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out things is to lay them out in order, which is to arrange them.

clue.text: Being weak and feeble, Conservative invested in awful money pit

indicators.note: money invested in something is placed inside it
an awful version is a mangled one, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: C is an abbreviation for Conservative
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A feeble Tory has put money into a hopeless venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotency is powerlessness, the state of lacking strength or effectiveness.

clue.text: Crop in yard that is left ultimately unsold

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is used

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for yard
ie stands for id est, that is
L is the abbreviation for left
the last letter of unsold

explanation.surface: Produce lying in a farmyard remains unsold.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm's yield is the amount of produce harvested, its crop.
